extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, patent practitioners/agents, and third-party requesters involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules from the MPEP governing papers, petitions, amendments, panel review, final actions, after-final practice, and appeals in ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsigned papers (filed by patent owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by owner which are unsigned or signed by less than all of the owners (no attorney of record or acting in representative capacity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsigned owner papers are defective and will be retained in the reexamination file; lack of signature can lead to denial of consideration unless remedied per applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service (owner submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by the patent owner in which no proof of service on requester is included and proof of service is required may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required proof of service when filing papers; absence may result in denial of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely papers (owner submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where owner has filed a paper which is untimely (filed after the period set for response), the paper will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure responses and papers are filed within the prescribed response period to be considered in the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsigned papers (filed by requester)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by requester which are unsigned will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must sign papers; unsigned submissions are treated as defective and may be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service (requester submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by requester in which no proof of service on owner is included and where proof of service is required may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party requesters must include proof of service on the patent owner when required to avoid denial of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party citations timing (storage file vs reexamination file)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions by third parties based solely on prior art patents or publications filed after the date of the order to reexamine are not entered into the patent file but delayed until the reexamination proceedings have been concluded; proper timely filed citations (filed prior to the order) are placed in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness relative to the order to reexamine determines whether third-party prior art is entered immediately or held in a storage file until conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party content appropriateness under 37 CFR 1.501
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper submitted by a third party is acceptable only if it raises only issues appropriate under 37 CFR 1.501 or consists solely of a prior decision on the patent by another forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions that go beyond the scope permitted by 1.501 may be excluded or treated as defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival/late-paper petition fees (35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing each petition for the revival of an unintentionally abandoned application or for an unintentionally delayed response in any reexamination proceeding, a revival fee applies ($1,620 unless filed under section 133 or 151, in which case $540).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must pay the applicable revival/late-paper fee; different fees apply depending on statutory basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival for unavoidable delay (37 CFR 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive for unavoidable delay must be accompanied by: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice, (2) the petition fee as set forth in §1.17(l), (3) a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that the entire delay in filing the required reply was unavoidable, and (4) any required terminal disclaimer (and fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unavoidable-delay petitions require detailed factual showing and evidence of the circumstances; must include the substantive reply and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival for unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive for unintentional delay must be accompanied by: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice, (2) the petition fee as set forth in §1.17(m), (3) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional (verified), and (4) any required terminal disclaimer (and fee); the Director may require additional information where doubt exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unintentional-delay petitions require a verified statement and the fee; Director may request further information to establish unintentionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration of denied revival petitions (timing and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application, a terminated or limited reexamination prosecution, or lapsed patent upon petition filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) must be filed within two months of the decision (unless the decision sets other time), and may be extended only under specified reexamination extension provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration timing is strict; renewed petitions have specific cover-letter titles ('Renewed Petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a)' or '(b)') and may be subject to only the limited extension avenues available in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration entitlement — patent owner response requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to be entitled to reconsideration, the patent owner must respond to the Office action (37 CFR 1.111(b)); the owner may respond with or without amendment and the patent will be reconsidered unless the action is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a response to an Office action is a prerequisite to entitlement to reconsideration; scope of permissible amendments depends on stage of prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical handling and entry of amendments (37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal instrument examiners and paralegals handle initial clerical processing; amendments complying with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) will be entered for purposes of reexamination in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow form and procedural rules in 1.530 when submitting amendments to ensure clerical entry; see MPEP §§2234 and 2250 for manner of entering amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter and claim-enlarging amendments (legal effect and treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new matter' amendment to the disclosure (35 U.S.C. 132) will be required to be canceled, and claims containing new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112. A 'new matter' amendment to the drawing is ordinarily not entered. Where an amendment enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent, the amendment will be entered; however the appropriate claims will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical entry does not equate to legal effect; beware of introducing new matter or enlarging claim scope—such changes trigger statutory rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for making a rejection final in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a final action, a clear issue should be developed; the examiner will provide the patent owner twice with information and references useful in defining the Office position. The first Office action should reflect consideration of arguments/ amendments and apply all relevant grounds of rejection; the second Office action will generally be made final. Criteria for finality are analogous to MPEP §706.07(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should fully develop and communicate issues; patent owners should respond thoroughly (including early presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131(a) or 1.132) to avoid premature final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review requirement and composition (MPEP §2271.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review will be conducted at each stage of the examiner's examination in an ex parte reexamination proceeding (except notices of informality or incomplete responses). The panel consists of three or more members: a manager, the examiner in charge, and a third member selected by the manager; conferees should be primary examiners or knowledgeable in the technology, and the majority should not have been involved in the original examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel review provides multi-examiner scrutiny to reduce bias and ensure comprehensive consideration; an original examiner should be a conferee only for justifiable reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel process and conferee participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must inform the manager of intent to issue an Office action; the manager convenes a panel which reviews the preliminary decision. If the conference confirms the examiner’s decision, the Office action is issued and signed by the examiner with two or more conferees initialing; all conferees initial even if dissenting. If not confirmed, the examiner reevaluates and issues an appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferees' initials document participation; disagreements may lead to reassignment of the proceeding if the examiner in charge disagrees with the conference decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and challenge period for failure to hold panel review
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is issued without panel review, the patent owner or third-party requester must promptly file a paper alerting the Office; any challenge must be made within two weeks of receipt of the Office action or it will not be considered. Failure to hold a panel review alone is not grounds to vacate Office decisions or restart the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely challenge is required; lack of panel review is not, by itself, dispositive of the action's validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for final Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: As with other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure final reexamination actions carry primary examiner signature to be procedurally proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art submitted by patent owner during prosecution (IDS effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where art is submitted in a prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501 and/or 1.555 and the submission is not accompanied by a statement similar to 37 CFR 1.97(e), the examiner may use the art and make the next Office action final (provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced based on new art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners should include appropriate statements when submitting art to avoid enabling an immediate final action; examiners may treat uncoupled art submissions as grounds to finalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final practice and amendment standards (37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, the patent owner no longer has right to unrestricted further prosecution. Consideration of amendments after final is governed by strict standards of 37 CFR 1.116 (before appeal) and 37 CFR 41.33 (after appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final are narrowly considered; parties should develop and present all issues and evidence prior to final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for entering amendments after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after final rejection and prior to the appeal brief may be entered if: (A) its total effect is to cancel claims or comply with a prior form requirement or present rejected claims in better form for appeal; or (B) for amendments touching merits, the patent owner provides a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented. The first proposed amendment after final will be given sufficient consideration and examiner will briefly explain reasons for not entering any part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First post-final amendment receives particular consideration; subsequent amendments are considered only to remove issues for appeal or to place a claim in patentable condition; examiner should notify which portions could be entered if filed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of defective responses after final (PTOL-467 vs PTOL-475)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices of giving time to supply omission (MPEP §2266.01) or notifying of defects via PTOL-475 (MPEP §2266.02) do not apply after a final Office action. If a defective (informal) response is filed after final rejection, the examiner should issue an advisory Office action (form PTOL-467) with an explanation rather than PTOL-475.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTOL-467 to explain defects after final rejection; do not apply pre-final remedial forms and time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and limits in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may appeal adverse decisions to the Board and seek court review; a third-party requester may not appeal or participate in the patent owner's appeal. For reexaminations filed before Nov. 29, 1999 appeals could be taken after the second rejection; for those filed on/after that date appeals are allowed only after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the filing-date-based distinctions for when an appeal may be taken and that third parties lack appeal rights in ex parte reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal need not be signed but must be accompanied by the fee required by 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1). The filing period for the notice of appeal is the period set for response in the last Office action (normally 2 months). A timely first response to a final rejection with a shortened statutory period is construed as including a request to extend the period for an additional month (but not beyond six months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File appeals and pay fees within prescribed response periods; timely responses can effect a one-month extension where allowable but cannot exceed six months total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective appeal handling and cure period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a notice of appeal is defective (e.g., no proof of service, wrong proceeding), the patent owner will be notified using form PTOL-475 with explanation and given a one-month (or 30 days, whichever is longer) period to cure defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defective appeals can be cured within the specified cure period; timely correction preserves appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to file timely notice of appeal or fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner does not timely file a notice of appeal and/or the appropriate appeal fee, the appeal is dismissed, the reexamination prosecution is terminated, and a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) will be issued indicating claim status at time of final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting appeal filing and fee deadlines is critical—failure terminates the reexamination and leads toward certificate issuance reflecting current claim status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief timing and amendments related to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal brief must be filed within 2 months from the date of the appeal. Amendments should not be included in the appeal brief; separate amendments not included with the brief are governed by MPEP §1207. Extensions for filing the appeal brief may be requested via petition (usually 1 month) to the CRU or TC with fee; extensions beyond 1 month require extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include substantive amendments within the brief; use proper petition procedures for extensions and file amendment papers separately as necessary.
